experiments.model: Primary mouse lung endothelial cells from male C57BL/6 donors3-4weeks, passages3-4; Ad-KLK8 MOI1,3,10 for48h vs adenovector. Mouse intratracheal Ad-KLK8 1x10^8pfu/30µL,48h vs vector.
experiments.n: cells n4; mouse tissues n6; RNAseq plot shows3 columns per group but legend does not explicitly define biological n
experiments.result: KLK8 overexpression reduces MTT signal, increases FITC-dextran permeability, reduces VE-cadherin/pAkt/FOXM1, yields shed VE-cadherin fragment; in vivo increases EBA leak and injury. RNAseq regulator/pathway associations are predictions.
experiments.limits: KLK8-overexpression injury is not BUB1B-deficient disease; MTT is metabolic viability proxy, not direct cell counting.

experiments.role: genetic rescue, sole direct Bub1b measurement
experiments.model: MLVECs; Len-FOXM1 MOI10 for30min before Ad-vector/KLK8 MOI3 for48h; EdU10µM for2h
experiments.result: FOXM1 overexpression partially restores EdU-positive cells and Ccnd1/Cdc20/Ccnf/Bub1b mRNA under KLK8 overexpression. EdU visually~6% to~17% vs~26% vector baseline; Bub1b mRNA~0.5 to~0.8 relative to1.0 baseline; rescue comparisons **P<0.01. Estimates are visual.
experiments.bub1b_limits: No BUBR1 protein, localization, spindle-assembly checkpoint, chromosome segregation, aneuploidy or variant-specific function measured. No antibody or SC79 arm measures Bub1b.
experiments.limits: Group means remain below vector-control means; no direct baseline-versus-rescue equivalence test is shown.

experiments.role: administered chemical Akt activator; mechanistic positive probe
experiments.dose_timing: 10µM in presence/absence of Ad-KLK8 MOI3; readout48h; exact addition interval unspecified
experiments.result: Restores pAkt/Akt and FOXM1 protein to approximately untreated-vector baseline during KLK8 overexpression; increases basal FOXM1. FigS8D **P<0.01.
experiments.limits: No SC79 animal dosing/survival, leak assay, EdU, Bub1b/BUBR1 or fidelity measurement; do not inherit antibody benefit.

experiments.role: administered mTOR agonist negative pathway probe
experiments.result: Raises p-mTOR and p-S6K but does not restore FOXM1. Not a positive restorative lead from this paper.
experiments.limits: MHY1485 S8E shows phospho-mTOR/phospho-S6K normalized with beta-actin but no total-mTOR/total-S6K denominators; do not claim a phosphorylation-fraction comparison.

experiments.dose_timing: 10µM;48h endpoint; VE-cadherin lentivirus MOI10 for30min before Ad-KLK8 MOI3 in rescue experiments
experiments.result: VE-cadherin overexpression restores pAkt/FOXM1; AZD5363 substantially blocks the VE-cadherin-associated FOXM1 increase. Not a restorative result for AZD5363.

strengths: Two injury models and pharmacological/genetic direction agreement
Functional LPS vascular leak and short-term whole-animal survival outcomes beyond markers
Randomization stated; genotype/treatment blinded during measurement/analysis; pathology scored by two blinded pathologists
limitations: Pre-injury intervention only; no delayed treatment after established pulmonary injury.
Short follow-up ends48h; no sustained recovery, lung mechanics, blood gases, exercise or muscle function.
No plasma/lung antibody concentrations, half-life, occupancy, catalytic activity suppression, dose-response or antibody-independent pharmacological replication.
No antibody+endothelial FOXM1 loss-of-function epistasis proving that survival depends on this pathway; systemic immune/other-organ effects remain possible.

Saline/sham antibody baseline arms help contextualize acute lung endpoints but are not a comprehensive toxicity assessment. No dedicated infection clearance, long-term growth, tumor initiation/progression, or genomic-instability controls.
All animal experiments male. Mouse experimental ages/strain/weights incompletely specified; sample-size calculations/exclusions and exact survival statistics not provided.
No BUB1B-mutant, BubR1-hypomorphic, MVA, patient-derived, or N1002K model; actual patient variant phase and N1002K function remain unknown.
Human cross-reactivity/neutralization and final clinical formulation not established by the reviewed study.
source_corrections: Fig1 legend title omits inhibition, reversing plain-language direction; experimental groups/body identify inhibitory antibody as beneficial.
FigS10 title says KLK8 deficiency, but legend/panels use neutralizing antibody, not knockout.
Main text says FOXM1 overexpression restored proliferation; S7 rescue group means remain below vector-control means; no baseline-versus-rescue equivalence test is supplied.
Main text refers to figure administration and supplement RNAseq methods to Fig7E; stale references do not supply additional data.
Fig1J body estimates shed VE-cadherin~30kDa; image labels35kDa. Preserve approximate30-35kDa rather than precise cleavage-site claim.

comparison_to_existing_project_candidate.scope: Evidence-level comparison only; comparator primary papers not rereviewed in this bounded task.
comparison_to_existing_project_candidate.niacin: Existing project niacin evidence includes human functional observations but no established MVA rescue; antibody has controlled mouse organ/survival protection in a different disease. Neither is a direct MVA efficacy demonstration.
comparison_to_existing_project_candidate.apitegromab: Existing project apitegromab randomized motor evidence in treated SMA is more directly functional in humans, but transfers neither to MVA nor endothelial biology. Antibody remains a worthwhile independent preclinical organ-protection lead.
comparison_to_existing_project_candidate.conclusion: Retain KLK8 antibody positive signal without requiring it to defeat nominees; current evidence does not justify prioritizing it as a human MVA treatment. Do not infer harm solely from higher FOXM1/proliferation.

source_cautions: Figure 3A-B caption says K858 but actual panel labels and Results show siKif11; actual drug EdU panels are 3F-G.
Figure 2A GSEA displays FDR=0.3435; not a significant pathway-enrichment claim.
S2B legend calls the plot cell-cycle phases although plotted endpoint is apoptotic rate.
S2C-D legend states rapamycin 20 nM and 24 h followed by PDGF-BB 24 h, while plot labels show 0/12/24/48 h; retain this timing discrepancy. It is KIF11 reduction, not BUBR1 rescue.
No VSMC-specific in vivo manipulation or uninjured K858 arm; systemic contributions unresolved.
No PK, pediatric exposure, MVA genotype, muscle output or checkpoint-restoration measurement.

Figure 3H CCK8 data extend through 72 h despite caption wording of a 24 h PDGF-BB treatment; Figure 3C and 4H also show 0/24/48/72 h time courses. Do not assign every plotted result to a 24 h exposure.
Figure 3F-G caption calls the assay CCK8, but actual panels show EdU images and EdU-positive-cell percentage.
Figure 4 caption/results swap some protein and flow-cytometry panel references: actual protein blots/quantification are D-E and actual flow/cell-phase panels are F-G.
assessment.decision: Retain vascular antiproliferative tool evidence; decline present MVA restoration or muscle-compensation lead. No universal class-level contraindication inferred.

drug_results.regimen: Default 1 micromolar rhGAA for final 3 days

drug_results.model: Pom1b, Pom2b and Pom3a iPSC-derived myocyte clones, one selected clone per patient line, with within-clone untreated/treated comparisons
drug_results.regimen: Default 1 micromolar Myozyme rhGAA for final 3 days of differentiation
drug_results.n: 3 microscopic fields per comparison; not 3 independent treatment experiments or additional patients
drug_results.denominator: Integrated MitoTracker Red fluorescence adjusted for MHC-positive area; treatment fold change relative to the same clone without rhGAA
drug_results.result: rhGAA significantly decreased MitoTracker MFI in Pom1b and Pom3a (both P<0.01), with no significant change in Pom2b. Untreated Pompe-versus-control MFI comparison was not significant.
drug_results.scope: Actual drug-associated staining change; does not independently demonstrate restored mitochondrial respiration, contractile force or general mitochondrial function.

controls.rapamycin: 200 nM for 1 h before stimulation, used to verify phosphorylation readouts; not a disease-rescue experiment.
controls.doxycycline: MyoD induction, 1 microgram/mL; not a therapeutic test.
controls.bFGF_and_Y27632: Cell-culture reagents, not asserted disease treatment.

source_cautions: MyoD overexpression itself suppresses proliferation; authors state this model is unsuitable to analyze cell-cycle/proliferation pathways.
No CRISPR-isogenic control, muscle force, long-term renewal or MVA experiment.
No evidence that this MVA case is GAA-deficient; tissue overlap and BUB1B transcript increase do not establish an indication for GAA replacement.
Myozyme identity does not transfer effects to avalglucosidase or cipaglucosidase formulations.
Pom1 had only one GAA sequence variant identified despite profound enzymatic deficiency; patient groups were not claimed to be fully sequence-solved.
assessment.decision: Retain as a positive lesion-matched enzyme-replacement model and drug-associated BUB1B-transcript observation. Decline direct MVA nomination absent a GAA-deficiency bridge.
